title: Stream Processing: CDC, Windows & Effectively-Once
summary: Replay a database change log into a table idempotently, aggregate events into event-time tumbling windows with a watermark and allowed lateness, and build a consumer that survives a crash without losing or double-counting messages.

hints.test_cdc_applies_insert_update_delete: Ops 'c' and 'u' set state[key] = a copy of the 'after' image, and 'd' removes the key. Return the LSN of the last event you applied.
hints.test_cdc_skips_already_applied_lsns: Track the highest LSN applied so far and skip any event with lsn <= it. Replays after a connector restart and duplicates inside a batch both disappear that way.
hints.test_cdc_orders_events_by_lsn: The log position (LSN) is the source of truth for order. Sort the batch by lsn before applying.
hints.test_cdc_is_idempotent_and_pure: Start from a copy, {k: dict(v) for k, v in state.items()}, so the caller's state and the returned state never share row dicts.
hints.test_windows_use_event_time: Bucket by when the event happened, event_time - event_time % size, not by arrival_time. Processing time depends on network delays.
hints.test_late_events_dropped_after_watermark: Keep watermark = the max event_time accepted so far. An event is late when its window end (start + size) + allowed_lateness <= watermark. Return late events in arrival order.
hints.test_allowed_lateness_accepts_stragglers: allowed_lateness keeps a window open that much longer after the watermark passes its end, so slightly late events still count.
hints.test_consumer_processes_everything_and_c: Loop while store['offset'] < len(log): take log[offset:offset + batch_size], process every message, then set store['offset'] to the end of the batch.
hints.test_consumer_dedupes_redelivered_messag: Keep store['processed_ids']. If a message id is already in it, skip the message. Otherwise update the balance and add the id together.
hints.test_crash_restart_is_effectively_once: Commit the offset only AFTER the batch is processed. Committing first loses the rest of the batch on a crash (at-most-once). Committing after makes it at-least-once, and dedup by id makes the redelivery harmless.
